text: SideSight 为 DSH 的文本模型补充截图、图表、界面和视频理解能力，并提供 macOS 本地 OCR。它注册一个视觉模型适配器和 Web 设置页，将图像交给单独配置的多模态服务，再把文字证据返回给 DSH。可分析图片、比较界面差异、识别截图文字及抽取视频帧；本地 OCR 可离线处理。适合需要让编码 agent 理解视觉材料的 DSH 用户。云端分析需配置服务地址、模型和可选 API key；本地 OCR 仅支持 macOS。

SideSight adds vision analysis and local OCR to DSH. Its adapter registers a vision model and web settings panel, sends images to a provider, and returns text evidence. It analyzes charts, UI differences, and videos. Cloud use needs a provider URL and model; local OCR requires macOS.

Can my text-only coding agent inspect a screenshot?
I need local OCR for an image without configuring a cloud model.
SideSight 的功能「分析截图与图片」：CLI 接收图片和具体问题，调用配置的视觉模型并返回文本回答与证据，可按需检查原图裁剪区域。
SideSight 的功能「本地 OCR」：明确选择 local 后，在 macOS 上调用 Vision 识别图片文字并返回文本及区域证据；该路径只处理 OCR。
SideSight 的功能「视频分析」：输入视频后优先发送给支持视频的 provider，否则用 ffmpeg 抽取有序帧，再将画面和时间信息交给模型。
SideSight 的功能「DSH 附图理解」：视觉模型适配器读取 DSH 附件，将分析结果转换为文本证据供原文本模型继续处理。
SideSight 的功能「Web 设置」：在 DSH 设置页填写 provider 地址、视觉模型和 API key，保存或清除密钥并查看是否已配置。
SideSight 使用前须知：云端图片分析会把媒体内容发送到用户配置的视觉 provider；可选择 macOS local OCR 执行本地文字识别。
SideSight 使用前须知：DSH 插件需填写 provider 地址和模型；视频若 provider 不支持原生视频输入，则需要系统可用的 ffmpeg 来抽取帧。

sidesight README · For DeepSeek Harness：SideSight supports both of DeepSeek Harness's native extension paths: a filesystem skill for the simplest installation, and a configurable plugin bundle. Neither path starts an MCP server.

sidesight README · Install as a configurable DSH plugin：In a DSH conversation, ask the agent:

> Please install ZhuXinAI/sidesight dsh plugin

Or directly run:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:ZhuXinAI/sidesight
```

Restart the profile after changing its configuration:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web
```

Open DSH Web Settings and choose the `SideSight` entry to fill in the Base URL, Vision model, and API key.

section: Install as a configurable DSH plugin

text: sidesight README · Install as a configurable DSH plugin：The plugin contributes the configured values to DSH-managed shell calls and the skill maps them to SideSight's `SIDESIGHT_BASE_URL`, `SIDESIGHT_API_KEY`, and `SIDESIGHT_MODEL` variables when it invokes `npx -y sidesight <command>`. The API key value is not interpolated into the command text or ordinary tool result, and the skill forbids inspecting or printing it. Treat the profile configuration as sensitive because a manually entered key is stored with that profile.
section: Install as a configurable DSH plugin

text: sidesight README · Install as a configurable DSH plugin：The pasted-image bridge uses the package's bundled `dist/cli.js` when available. A GitHub/source install does not contain that generated directory, so the plugin automatically falls back to `npx -y sidesight`; no separate manual CLI install in the DSH profile is required. The fallback needs `npx` and npm access or a cached SideSight package.
section: Install as a configurable DSH plugin

text:
sidesight README · Install as a filesystem skill：DeepSeek Harness natively discovers filesystem skills from `.dsh/skills/` in a project or `$DSH_HOME/skills/` (normally `~/.dsh/skills/`) for all projects. No adapter or core workflow change is required.

Install for the current project from its Git repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .dsh/skills && git clone https://github.com/ZhuXinAI/sidesight .dsh/skills/sidesight
```

Or install for all DSH projects:

sidesight README · Install as a filesystem skill：```bash
mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" && git clone https://github.com/ZhuXinAI/sidesight "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/sidesight"
```

The repository-level `SKILL.md` routes visual work directly to `npx -y sidesight image`, `ui`, `ocr`, `diagnose`, `diagram`, `chart`, `diff`, or `video`.

sidesight README · Enable attached-image vision in DSH：DSH checks the selected model's declared input modalities before it accepts an attached image. The original `deepseek-official` text route will therefore show “the current model does not support images” even when SideSight credentials are configured. After filling the SideSight Settings fields, choose a model from the added `DeepSeek (SideSight vision)` provider, for example `DeepSeek-V4-Flash (SideSight vision)`. The wrapper advertises image input to DSH, reads the durable attachment through DSH, sends it to SideSight, and forwards only bounded visual evidence to the original text model; the native thumbnail remains in the session log.

sidesight README · Enable attached-image vision in DSH：The attached-image bridge handles the exact durable attachment automatically. The SideSight skill does not ask the model to locate an attachment on disk or create a local copy. Native DSH image tooling remains available for an explicitly supplied local path, but it is not an attachment-recovery step. Keeping the original text route selected is expected to preserve DSH's image rejection; switch to the SideSight vision variant for attached images.

sidesight README · Enable attached-image vision in DSH：The attachment bridge uses the exact DSH attachment bytes in a private operating-system temporary directory and removes that temporary materialization after analysis. It does not silently replace an attachment with `clipboard`, `latest`, or an older workspace file, and it does not create a workspace copy. For a direct CLI call on an existing path outside the workspace, pass that file's containing directory as a scoped allowlist:

sidesight README · Enable attached-image vision in DSH：```bash
media_path="/absolute/path/to/image.png"
npx -y sidesight image "$media_path" \
  --allowed-dir "$(dirname "$media_path")" \
  --question "Describe this exact image"

For DSH plugin users, `npx sidesight setup` is optional. You do not need it when `baseUrl`, `apiKey`, and `model` are filled in through DSH. It remains available as a fallback when those fields are blank, and for filesystem-skill installations that prefer SideSight's owner-only saved configuration.
sidesight README · Enable attached-image vision in DSH：To install into another profile, replace `web` with that profile name. Remove the bundle with `dsh plugin --profile <name> remove sidesight`.

sidesight README · Install for coding agents：Give your coding agent this instruction:

```text
Read and install the SideSight skill from:
https://github.com/ZhuXinAI/sidesight/blob/main/SKILL.md
```

After the skill is installed, ask the agent:

```text
Help me configure SideSight for cloud vision.
```

sidesight README · Install for coding agents：The agent will direct you to run `npx sidesight setup` and wait for your confirmation. API keys stay in the hidden setup prompt or your environment; never paste a real key into the agent chat. The agent must not search shell profiles, `.env` files, keychains, home directories, or unrelated project files for credentials.

If you explicitly want offline or on-device OCR, say so directly:

```text
Use native on-device OCR for this screenshot; do not ask me to configure a cloud provider.
```
sidesight README · Install for coding agents：The agent should run `sidesight ocr <image> --provider local`. This path does not require cloud setup on macOS.

sidesight README · Direct use：Tell the agent what to inspect and what evidence you need:

```text
Look at /path/to/screenshot.png and tell me why the button is disabled.
```

```text

```

```text

```

```text

```

sidesight README · Direct use：The skill routes the request to the matching CLI command. Cloud-backed tasks use the configured multimodal provider; explicit local OCR uses macOS Vision and never makes a cloud request.
sidesight README · Optional MCP setup：Continue to [Cloud setup and key saving](#cloud-setup-and-key-saving), [local OCR](#explicit-local-ocr), [MCP](#mcp), or [Codex skill](#codex-skill) for details.

sidesight README · What SideSight does：SideSight gives a text-only coding model a safe, scriptable way to ask a separately configured multimodal model about screenshots, diagrams, charts, UI differences, and videos. For explicit OCR requests on macOS, it can use Apple Vision locally instead. The host agent receives concise text and structured evidence; it never needs native image support.

```text
Text-only coding agent
        │ shell command or MCP call
        ▼
SideSight

sidesight README · Install the CLI：SideSight targets Node.js 22 or newer.

```bash
pnpm add -g sidesight
sidesight --help
```

For a checkout:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
node dist/cli.js --help
```

sidesight README · Cloud setup and key saving：SideSight uses a separate provider configuration so it does not interfere with the host coding model:

```bash

sidesight README · The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.：npx sidesight setup
sidesight doctor
sidesight diagnose ./screenshots/error.png \
  --question "Transcribe the exact error and identify the likely source file"
```
section: The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.

text: sidesight README · The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.：The `opencode-go` preset uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` and model `mimo-v2.5`. A useful pairing is a text-first host coding model such as DeepSeek V4 Flash with MiMo-V2.5 for vision. Provider endpoints, model availability, pricing, retention, and policies can change; check the current [OpenCode Go documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/).
section: The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.

sidesight README · The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.：For a generic OpenAI-compatible provider:bash
sidesight setup \
  --profile generic \
  --base-url "https://provider.example/v1" \
  --model "your-vision-model" \
  --api-key "your-key"
```
section: The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.

text: sidesight README · The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.：Running `npx sidesight setup` without options opens an interactive walkthrough for the base URL, model, and API key. Existing profile, environment, and saved values are shown as defaults; press Enter to keep them. The API key prompt is hidden in a terminal. For scripts, pass the setup flags as shown above. Setup can be rerun; omitted values are preserved from the saved file or current environment. `SIDESIGHT_API_KEY` is the canonical secret variable, and SideSight also accepts `Z_AI_API_KEY` as a compatibility alias. `config show` reports only `apiKeyConfigured`; it never prints the saved key. Explicit local OCR does not use this setup.
section: The key is stored with mode 0600 under ~/.sidesight/config.json.

text:
sidesight README · Explicit local OCR：When the user explicitly requests local, offline, on-device, or native OCR, no cloud setup is needed:

```bash
sidesight ocr screenshot.png --provider local

sidesight README · Equivalent forms:：sidesight ocr screenshot.png --offline
sidesight ocr screenshot.png --ocr-backend system
```

sidesight README · Equivalent forms:：On macOS, SideSight invokes the bundled Swift bridge to Apple Vision text recognition. It returns the detected text, confidence when available, and normalized evidence regions. The image is processed on the device and no provider request or API key is used. This local route currently supports OCR only; UI interpretation, error diagnosis, diagrams, charts, diffs, and videos still require a configured cloud or private multimodal provider.

sidesight README · Equivalent forms:：If Swift or the Xcode Command Line Tools are unavailable, SideSight returns an actionable error. On other operating systems, the local route fails clearly rather than silently sending the image to the cloud.

sidesight README · CLI：```bash
sidesight image screenshot.png --question "What visual evidence explains the disabled button?"
sidesight ui design.png --question "Describe the layout and produce React and Tailwind guidance"
sidesight ocr dashboard.png --detail fine --question "Read the bottom-right metrics card"
sidesight ocr receipt.png --provider local --format json

sidesight README · CLI：Every task uses the same core engine. `--question -` reads a focused question from stdin. `--instructions-file` adds project guidance without replacing SideSight's internal safety rules. `--format json` writes exactly one JSON object to stdout; progress is sent to stderr. `--output` saves the rendered result as well as writing it to stdout.

sidesight README · CLI：Supported media sources are local PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF (first frame), MP4, MOV, M4V, and WebM files; HTTP/HTTPS URLs; and validated base64 data URIs. `sidesight image latest` reads the newest image from `SIDESIGHT_DROP_DIR` or `./screenshots`. `clipboard` is supported on macOS when `pbpaste -Prefer png` can read a bitmap.

sidesight README · CLI：Local paths are the preferred input for coding-agent workflows. A raw base64 string is not accepted; use a complete `data:<mime>;base64,...` URI. Codex/Claude image attachments are not automatically visible to the CLI as files, so export an attachment or clipboard image to a path (or provide a complete data URI) before invoking SideSight. The provider adapter creates base64 data URIs from validated media internally, but never logs them.

sidesight README · Configuration：Precedence is CLI flags, environment variables, saved user config, then profile defaults. `sidesight setup` writes provider settings to `~/.sidesight/config.json` with directory mode `0700` and file mode `0600`. Set `SIDESIGHT_CONFIG_DIR` or `SIDESIGHT_CONFIG_FILE` to use another location. Use `sidesight config init` to create a non-secret template and `sidesight config show` to inspect resolved values.

Important variables:

sidesight README · Configuration：```text
SIDESIGHT_API_KEY
SIDESIGHT_BASE_URL
SIDESIGHT_MODEL
SIDESIGHT_PROFILE

Provider compatibility at a glance:

sidesight README · Configuration：| Profile | Default endpoint | Default model | Images | Native video |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opencode-go` | OpenCode Go `/v1` | `mimo-v2.5` | OpenAI-compatible `image_url` | No; bounded ffmpeg frames |
| `generic` | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | `vision-model` | OpenAI-compatible `image_url` | No; bounded ffmpeg frames |
| `local` | on-device | `macos-vision` | macOS Vision OCR only | No |

sidesight README · Configuration：Any provider that accepts the documented OpenAI-compatible multimodal chat-completions shape can use `generic`.

`SIDESIGHT_ALLOWED_DIRS` is not required for the usual case: by default the current working directory is allowed. Set it when an image or video lives elsewhere, for example `export SIDESIGHT_ALLOWED_DIRS="$HOME/Screenshots:$PWD"` on Unix-like systems. Keeping the allowlist narrow prevents accidental access to unrelated local files.

sidesight README · Configuration：Normalized regions use `x,y,width,height` in the range `0..1`, measured from the full original image:

```bash
sidesight ocr screenshot.png --region 0.65,0.70,0.35,0.30 \
  --question "Read every visible character"
```

sidesight README · Configuration：`overview` makes one bounded pass. `normal`, `fine`, and `auto` may inspect a bounded full-resolution crop. Crops are always made from the original, never from a resized crop. Zoom rounds, provider calls, image count, dimensions, media sizes, video frames, and output tokens are bounded.

sidesight README · MCP：Run the stdio adapter with:

```bash
sidesight mcp

sidesight README · or, after publishing/installing the package:：The server exposes `ui_to_artifact`, `extract_text_from_screenshot`, `diagnose_error_screenshot`, `understand_technical_diagram`, `analyze_data_visualization`, `ui_diff_check`, `image_analysis`, and `video_analysis`. It uses the exact same configuration, prompts, media security, provider adapter, and core engine as the CLI. OCR tool calls may pass `backend: "local"` for macOS Vision without cloud setup. MCP protocol messages use stdout; diagnostics use stderr. Environment variables are inherited by `npx`; saved `~/.sidesight/config.json` settings are also resolved automatically.
sidesight README · or, after publishing/installing the package:：For a copy-paste client configuration, use the MCP setup in [Optional MCP setup](#optional-mcp-setup) above.

sidesight README · Codex skill：The single routing skill is the repository-level `SKILL.md`, shared by DSH and the installer. Install it into a user skill directory with:

```bash
node scripts/install-skill.mjs "$HOME/.agents/skills"
```

The installer copies real files and does not create symlinks. The skill prefers DOM, accessibility trees, logs, and source data when those are available, then routes visual questions to the smallest appropriate SideSight command.

sidesight README · Codex skill：If you are asking an agent to install the skill, use this prompt:

> Read and install the skill here at [SKILL.md](https://github.com/ZhuXinAI/sidesight/blob/main/SKILL.md).

sidesight README · Security and privacy：Media is untrusted input. Local paths are canonicalized against an allowlist, symlink escapes are rejected, file size and image dimensions are bounded, and MIME type is checked against magic bytes. Remote URLs are limited to HTTP/HTTPS, resolved and checked against private, localhost, and cloud-metadata networks, downloaded with timeouts and response-size limits, and revalidated across redirects. URLs embedded in media are returned only as evidence; they are never fetched.

sidesight README · Security and privacy：Cloud-backed images and videos are transmitted to the configured vision provider. Use a local or private OpenAI-compatible provider for sensitive screenshots, or use explicit `--provider local` for macOS OCR. API keys, authorization headers, data URIs, and full provider payloads are redacted from normal diagnostics. Vision output is untrusted evidence; SideSight never executes commands or modifies files based on it.

sidesight README · Doctor and troubleshooting：```bash
sidesight doctor
sidesight doctor --live
```

The default doctor checks Node.js, configuration, key presence, endpoint reachability, `sharp`, ffmpeg, allowed directories, and temporary storage without making a billable model call. `--live` sends a tiny deterministic image to the selected provider. Video frame sampling requires ffmpeg; install it or set `SIDESIGHT_FFMPEG_PATH`.

sidesight README · Doctor and troubleshooting：Provider failures are normalized: authentication, rate limits, invalid JSON, unreachable endpoints, and text-only-model image rejection produce actionable nonzero errors. A text-only backend cannot be used as the vision model; select a multimodal model through `SIDESIGHT_MODEL`.

sidesight README · Development and tests：```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm format:check
pnpm lint
pnpm typecheck

Live checks are opt-in and require credentials; they are not part of ordinary CI.

To exercise all eight tasks against a configured provider, run `pnpm build` and then `SIDESIGHT_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live`. Without the opt-in flag or the three required provider variables, the script reports a skip and exits successfully.

sidesight README · Publishing：The first npm publication and the subsequent OIDC-based GitHub Actions release flow are documented in [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md). Releases run only for matching `vX.Y.Z` tags.

sidesight README · License and reference material：SideSight is MIT licensed. Its architecture is informed by the public [Z.AI Vision MCP documentation](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/mcp/vision-mcp-server), the MIT-licensed [vision-mcp reference](https://github.com/Pelican0126/vision-mcp), [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/), and the [Codex skills documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/build-skills). SideSight uses original prompt templates and does not copy private provider prompts.
